title: Suitable test data
starter: A program asks for a school year group from 7 to 11. Suggest five pieces of test data for it, and explain what each one is testing.
starterAnswer: Accept any sensible attempt: this is a hook, not an assessment.
Look for the vocabulary from the lesson objectives appearing in students' own words.
Students who are stuck should still write something: the experience will correct it.
starterNote: Take two or three answers, then leave it open. Come back to it in the plenary, when they can answer it properly.

stations.name: Why test with different data?
facts: A program that works for one input may still fail for others.
A test plan lists each test, the data used, the type of test and the expected result.
Good testing covers valid, invalid and erroneous inputs.
stations.challenge: What makes a good testing strategy?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A program that works for one input may still fail for others.
Also credit: A test plan lists each test, the data used, the type of test and the expected result.

questions.q: Why should a program be tested with lots of different data?
questions.a: It may work for some inputs but fail for others

questions.q: What does a test plan include for each test?
questions.a: The test data, the type of test and the expected result

stations.name: Normal data
facts: Typical, valid data that the program should accept.
For a school-age field from 11 to 19: 14.
stations.challenge: Give two more examples of normal data for an age from 11 to 19.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Typical, valid data that the program should accept.
Also credit: For a school-age field from 11 to 19: 14.

questions.q: Which is normal data for an age from 11 to 19?
What should happen when normal data is entered?

stations.name: Boundary data
facts: Valid data on the very edge of the accepted range.
For an age from 11 to 19: 11 and 19.
Boundaries are where programmers most often make mistakes, like < instead of <=.
stations.challenge: What are the boundary values for a canteen menu that accepts 1 to 4?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Valid data on the very edge of the accepted range.
Also credit: For an age from 11 to 19: 11 and 19.

questions.q: Which is boundary data for an age from 11 to 19?
Why is boundary data so important to test?
questions.a: Mistakes like using < instead of <= only show up at the edges

stations.name: Invalid data
facts: Data of the correct type, but outside the accepted range.
For an age from 11 to 19: 24 or -3.
stations.challenge: Give an example of invalid data for a month number.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Data of the correct type, but outside the accepted range.
Also credit: For an age from 11 to 19: 24 or -3.

questions.q: Which is invalid data for an age from 11 to 19?
What should a robust program do with invalid data?

stations.name: Erroneous data
facts: Data of the wrong type that should be rejected.
Without a type check, erroneous data can crash a program.
stations.challenge: What would happen to a program that doubles a number if the user typed 'five'?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Data of the wrong type that should be rejected.
Also credit: For an age from 11 to 19: 'fourteen'.

questions.q: Which is erroneous data for an age from 11 to 19?
What's the difference between invalid and erroneous data?
questions.a: Invalid is the right type but out of range; erroneous is the wrong type

stations.name: Test a comment box
facts: A comment box allows up to 200 characters.
Test just under, exactly at, and just over the limit.
The program should show how many characters are left, or how many are over.
stations.challenge: Fill in five tests for the comment box on your worksheet.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A comment box allows up to 200 characters.
Also credit: Test just under, exactly at, and just over the limit.

questions.q: Which is boundary data for a 200-character limit?
A canteen menu accepts 1 to 4. What should happen if 5 is entered?
questions.a: It is rejected and the user is asked again

final.name: Final challenge: sort the test data

questions.q: Which type of test data is each input for a score from 0 to 100?
questions.a: 14 = Normal; 16 = Normal; 11 = Boundary; 19 = Boundary; 24 = Invalid; -3 = Invalid; fourteen = Erroneous; N/A = Erroneous

final.note: Students should have predicted these on the worksheet before tapping the star. Mark the prediction, not just the final answer.

exam.q: A booking form accepts a number of tickets from 1 to 6. Give four pieces of test data, name the type of each, and state why the test is needed.
points: A test plan lists each test, the data used, the type of test and the expected result.
Typical, valid data that the program should accept.
Valid data on the very edge of the accepted range.
Data of the correct type, but outside the accepted range.
Data of the wrong type that should be rejected.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark per point, to a maximum of 8.

common: Naming a term without saying what it does: most questions need the term and its purpose.
Answering 'it's faster' or 'it's better' with no reason: link it to the characteristic the question is about.
Repeating the question in the answer and stopping there.
